company.name: Lowe's Companies, Inc.
company.employees: Approximately 167,000 full-time and 109,000 part-time associates as of January 30, 2026 [s3]
company.fiscalYearEnd: Friday nearest January 31; fiscal 2025 ended January 30, 2026 [s3]
company.industry: Home improvement retail and Pro building-products distribution [s3][s4]
company.summary: Lowe's is an omnichannel home-improvement retailer with 1,761 stores and a growing Pro distribution footprint [s1][s4]. Its near-term agenda combines FBM and ADG integration, continued digital and AI investment, and operating discipline amid soft discretionary DIY demand [s1][s4][s25].

overview.whatTheyDo: Lowe's sells home-improvement products and services through stores and digital channels and serves professional customers through Lowe's Pro Supply, FBM, ADG, and related capabilities [s3][s4][s25].

scale.label: Retail selling space
scale.value: 196.0 million square feet as of July 31, 2026

scale.label: Pro distribution branches
scale.value: More than 540 U.S. and Canadian branches as of January 30, 2026

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Non-reportable operations include FBM's Ceilings and Wall Systems and Commercial Doors and Hardware businesses and ADG's Interior Finishes business.

trends.trajectory: Growth is being led by Pro, online, and home services while discretionary DIY demand remains soft. Acquisitions expand Lowe's addressable Pro market but are currently adding integration work and margin dilution [s1][s4][s25].

industry.trend: Remodeling growth is forecast to slow to 0.5% by the second quarter of 2027.
industry.implication: Broad technology programs face a higher proof threshold; engineering work should tie directly to conversion, margin, or operating leverage.

industry.trend: DIY's share of improvement spending fell to 15.9% in 2023 while professional spending grew from 2021 through 2023.
industry.implication: Integrated Pro quoting, ordering, credit, product-substitution, and fulfillment workflows become more strategically important.

industry.trend: Remodeler input costs rose 6.6% year over year in Q2 2026 and had risen for 11 consecutive quarters.
industry.implication: Pro systems need current cost, availability, substitution, quote-validity, and margin controls.

pressures.evidence: Management moved its annual outlook to the low end of its prior range while Pro, online, and home services offset softer discretionary DIY demand.
Q1 gross margin fell 70 basis points, with adjusted operating-margin pressure attributed primarily to acquisition dilution.
Lowe's eliminated about 600 corporate and support roles, less than 1% of its workforce, to redirect resources toward stores.

catalysts.event: Lowe's completed its acquisition of Artisan Design Group.
catalysts.whyItMatters: ADG adds another acquired Pro platform and operating estate whose workflows may need integration.

catalysts.event: Lowe's completed its $8.8 billion acquisition of Foundation Building Materials.
catalysts.whyItMatters: FBM added 370 locations and a separate distribution and digital estate, creating a current integration boundary.

catalysts.event: Lowe's announced the elimination of about 600 corporate and support roles.
catalysts.whyItMatters: Technology teams face pressure to complete integration and modernization work with fewer central resources.

catalysts.event: Lowe's launched AI-driven material lists for Pro quotes.
catalysts.whyItMatters: Generative AI now sits in a revenue workflow where reliability, product data, and governance matter.

catalysts.event: Target announced that Chandhu Nair, Lowe's SVP of data, AI, and innovation, would become Target's chief AI officer.
catalysts.whyItMatters: The departure preceded a consolidation of Lowe's information and AI leadership.

catalysts.event: Five EVP appointments took effect, including Seemantini Godbole as EVP and chief information and AI officer.
catalysts.whyItMatters: A newly enlarged executive remit now spans technology, engineering, product, data, analytics, innovation, and AI.

catalysts.event: Lowe's launched a drone-delivery pilot with Wing and DoorDash in Matthews, North Carolina.
catalysts.whyItMatters: A new fulfillment channel introduces another customer-order integration and operational-control surface.

stack.evidence: Lowe's public GitHub organization exposes JVM audit tooling, a Kafka MirrorMaker lag exporter, a virtual-file-system library, and a Backstage fork.
Lowe's has used Google Cloud to replace a legacy technology stack and support Lowes.com and broader software delivery.
Google describes Lowe's use of Vertex AI Vector Search and visual AI for ecommerce recommendations.
Lowe's built Mylow and Mylow Companion with OpenAI.
Lowe's uses NVIDIA technology for store digital-twin work.

stack.technology: Oracle Fusion AI Data Platform and OCI
stack.evidence: Lowe's selected Oracle Fusion AI Data Platform, Autonomous AI Warehouse, and OCI for finance analytics, with KPMG assisting implementation.

patterns.theirEstate: Public evidence supports a JVM, Kafka, and Backstage-adjacent open-source footprint. Private repository scale, ownership, and review queues are not public.
Lowe's has an established Google Cloud modernization program, while FBM and ADG add current acquisition-integration boundaries. Their application maps and decommission plans are not public.
The cybersecurity risk envelope and security-operations vendor are public, but no public source establishes Lowe's CVE volume, patch SLA, dependency scanner, or remediation queue.

fit.summary: Lowe's has a large software-dependent retail estate, named modernization and acquisition-integration work, a newly consolidated AI mandate, and demonstrated willingness to use outside platforms. The pursuit still depends on proving a named backlog, control path, and budget route.

rubric.rationale: The 1,761-store omnichannel estate, more than 540 Pro branches, public software hiring, and open-source footprint imply substantial software operations, but engineering headcount and repository count are not public.
Lowe's has a named Google Cloud legacy-replacement program and must integrate the FBM and ADG estates.
Lowe's handles personal and payment-card information and maintains a global cybersecurity program, though no public source quantifies its application-remediation backlog.
Seemantini Godbole was newly appointed chief information and AI officer with an enterprise remit covering technology, engineering, product, data, analytics, innovation, and AI.
Fiscal 2026 capital-expenditure guidance is up to approximately $2.5 billion and acquisition integration is current, but the applicable software budget and procurement calendar are not public.

Lowe's has active relationships with Google Cloud, OpenAI, NVIDIA, Mirakl, Oracle, KPMG, and ReliaQuest, showing outside-vendor adoption; repository-access and AI-governance requirements remain unknown.

reasonsFor.point: A newly appointed executive owns both information technology and AI.
reasonsFor.evidence: Godbole's expanded remit took effect September 1, 2026.

reasonsFor.point: Acquisition integration creates bounded, business-visible workflows.
reasonsFor.evidence: FBM added 370 locations, while ADG added a nationwide design, distribution, and installation business.

reasonsFor.point: The software estate is heterogeneous enough for cross-tool engineering work.
reasonsFor.evidence: Public evidence spans Google Cloud, OpenAI, Vertex AI, Oracle, NVIDIA, Mirakl, and ReliaQuest.

reasonsAgainst.point: Cost pressure could delay a new platform purchase.
reasonsAgainst.evidence: Lowe's eliminated about 600 corporate and support roles and guided to approximately flat fiscal 2026 comparable sales.

reasonsAgainst.point: Powerful incumbents may already cover the target workflow.
reasonsAgainst.evidence: Google Cloud and OpenAI are established AI partners, and Lowe's actual coding assistant is not public.

reasonsAgainst.point: No buyer-confirmed engineering pain or security path is public.
reasonsAgainst.evidence: The reviewed sources do not name a late backlog, repository-access standard, coding assistant, or remediation queue.

disqualifiers: Lowe's will not name a specific backlog, business date, accountable owner, and measurable baseline before technical work.
Security or AI governance cannot approve any deployment pattern that permits useful work on representative code.
No budget owner, procurement route, or conditional paid next step is documented before a free proof begins.

competition.position: Primary documented engineering-platform and retail-AI incumbent.
competition.tradeoff: Google is better positioned where Lowe's work, identity, data, and models already live in Google Cloud and Vertex AI.

competition.position: Product-AI incumbent supporting Mylow and Mylow Companion.
competition.tradeoff: OpenAI has an approved relationship and direct experience with Lowe's customer and associate AI products.

competition.position: Finance analytics platform and implementation incumbents.
competition.tradeoff: They are better positioned for finance-data workloads and implementation work already centered on Oracle Fusion and OCI.
NVIDIA is better positioned for Omniverse-based simulation and digital-twin workloads.
Mirakl owns specialized marketplace capabilities and an existing integration surface.
ReliaQuest already operates inside Lowe's security processes and has established telemetry and response workflows.

competition.position: Credible alternative because Lowe's already develops AI products and engineering-platform capabilities.
competition.tradeoff: Internal teams have estate knowledge, approved access, and no incremental vendor review.

objections.objection: We already use Google and OpenAI.
objections.response: Treat those as the expected architecture. Test whether the incumbent workflow already completes one governed engineering task across the repository, ticket, CI, and review systems, and stop if it clears Lowe's threshold.

objections.objection: Security will not allow source code into another model.
objections.response: Let security define the boundary first. Begin read-only, document every data path and retention rule, prohibit secrets and production actions, and require human approval.

objections.objection: FBM integration is too important for a pilot.
objections.response: Do not start on a critical cutover. Choose a representative low-blast-radius issue with production-like standards, explicit acceptance tests, and rollback.

objections.objection: We reduced corporate roles and cannot absorb another tool.
objections.response: Use one owned backlog and one measurement plan. End the test if setup or review work rises without accepted work being completed.
First establish a defensible unit: one comparable issue moved from ready for engineering to an approved change. Scale only after Lowe's supplies its own volume and cost inputs.

dealModel.unit: One comparable, buyer-accepted issue moved from ready for engineering to an approved change, including implementation, tests, review, and rework.
assumptions: Illustrative planning assumption, not a Lowe's baseline: 15 comparable accepted issues in one quarter.
Illustrative planning assumption, not a Lowe's baseline: 24 active engineer-hours per issue before the pilot.
Illustrative planning assumption, not a Lowe's commitment: 16.8 active engineer-hours per pilot issue, representing a 30% reduction.
Illustrative planning assumption, not a Factory quote: $2,400 per seat per year.
Lowe's must replace all workload, effort, cost, threshold, and price inputs before using the model for a purchase decision.

ladder.gate: Written exit criterion, representative low-blast-radius issue, approved data boundary, baseline, and conditional paid-pilot decision.
Sourcing confirms the legitimate procurement route, scope is signed, baseline is captured, and the buyer pre-agrees the measured and control thresholds.
The pilot clears its written threshold without worsening defects or security outcomes, finance accepts the method, and a funded service group is named.
Security, privacy, architecture, identity, logging, support, and model-routing controls are approved at scale and two teams reproduce the result.
Lowe's finance accepts its bottom-up case, procurement selects an enterprise vehicle, adoption is funded, and portfolio governance is operational.
